podcast.body: A rock radio staple from Pearl Jam's debut album "Ten." Its consistent airplay was a significant factor in the album's eventual double platinum success. "driven by the singles Alive and Evenflow, both rock radio staples."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia
Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.body: After Eddie Vedder was invited to Seattle, the new band, then called Mookie Blaylock, went into the studio. By this point, "Dollar Short" had been renamed "Alive," and this demo was a "proper demo" that led to Mookie Blaylock securing a record deal. "And when Mookie Blaylock made a proper demo, it sounded like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Following the Mookie Blaylock demo and securing a record deal, the band changed its name to Pearl Jam. This demo represents the next stage in the song's evolution before its final release on the *Ten* album. "By the next round of demos, they had changed their name to Pearl Jam and Alive sounded like this."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song is from Pearl Jam's debut album, "Ten," released on August 27, 1991, a pivotal record in the rise of grunge. "Pearl Jam and Alive, their debut record 10 released on August 27th, 1991."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
